# Breakout Candidates

**Summary.** The best breakout bets for our league are players with a clear new role: a high-usage teammate is gone or they are in year two or year three. Buy them in the middle and late auction before the market prices the jump in. The core targets are Matas Buzelis, Austin Reaves, Brandon Miller, Darius Garland, Paul George and Jaren Jackson Jr., with cheap year-two and year-three bets behind them. In the first two weeks, check minutes, free throw rate and assist rate, and sell players whose role shrinks before stars return.

## Where breakouts come from

Usage and minutes carry over strongly from one season to the next. Usage holds at 0.83 and minutes per game at 0.78. So a breakout rarely comes from a player simply getting better. It comes from a role change: an injury, a trade or a free agency departure that frees up shots. One expert adds that most busts and breakouts come from injuries and random shooting seasons, not from changes in counting stats. For our auction, pay for a role that has already changed, not for hope. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=534), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=436))

The clearest openings are on teams that lost high-usage players and brought in fewer than they lost. The leftover usage has to go somewhere. Charlotte lost LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, which opens shots for Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and Naz Reid. Sacramento lost DeRozan, Westbrook and Schroder, which helps Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Keegan Murray. The Clippers lost Kawhi Leonard and James Harden, which leaves Darius Garland and Brandon Ingram as the top options. The Lakers lost LeBron, which opens usage and assists for Austin Reaves. ([07-01](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=855), [Brandon Miller](../profiles/players/brandon-miller.md), [Kon Knueppel](../profiles/players/kon-knueppel.md), [Naz Reid](../profiles/players/naz-reid.md), [Domantas Sabonis](../profiles/players/domantas-sabonis.md), [Zach LaVine](../profiles/players/zach-lavine.md), [Keegan Murray](../profiles/players/keegan-murray.md), [Darius Garland](../profiles/players/darius-garland.md), [Brandon Ingram](../profiles/players/brandon-ingram.md), [Austin Reaves](../profiles/players/austin-reaves.md))

A player who was third in line next to two stars can jump once one star leaves, mostly in assist rate. Paul George fits this pattern. With Jaylen Brown gone, he moves from third option to clear number two behind Jayson Tatum, with usage projected at 26, up from 23. Before you bid, check how he played in games with only one of the stars on the floor. ([07-01](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=892), [Paul George](../profiles/players/paul-george.md), [Jayson Tatum](../profiles/players/jayson-tatum.md))

Always check the usage picture first. More high-usage stars on a roster means fewer chances for role players, not more. Trae Young shares the ball with Davis and Dybantsa. Jaren Jackson Jr. shares it with Markkanen, George and Peterson. Dejounte Murray shares it with Jeremiah Fears on a crowded roster. Matas Buzelis shares it with Powell and Wilson. Any of these roles can turn out smaller than the projection. ([07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=783), [Trae Young](../profiles/players/trae-young.md), [Jaren Jackson Jr.](../profiles/players/jaren-jackson.md), [Dejounte Murray](../profiles/players/dejounte-murray.md), [Matas Buzelis](../profiles/players/matas-buzelis.md))

## Year two and year three

In recent years the big breakouts have moved to year two. Players who did not take a step in year two are the ones who tend to break out in year three. Young players usually get more usage and minutes each year, from a small rookie role to a bigger one by year three. Big jumps in year four are unlikely for players who showed nothing in their first three seasons. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=139), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=157), [09-10](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1602), [08-18](https://youtu.be/FxaSnyk9g90?t=1179))

The year-two names in our pool are Cooper Flagg, Dylan Harper, Cedric Coward, Collin Murray-Boyles and Egor Dëmin. Harper is expected to move into the starting lineup. Coward should get more minutes and shots. Murray-Boyles's usage is projected to go from 15% to about 18%. Dëmin is projected to start at shooting guard. The year-three names are Matas Buzelis, Ausar Thompson and Zach Edey. Experts expect a step from each of them. ([Cooper Flagg](../profiles/players/cooper-flagg.md), [Dylan Harper](../profiles/players/dylan-harper.md), [Cedric Coward](../profiles/players/cedric-coward.md), [Collin Murray-Boyles](../profiles/players/collin-murray-boyles.md), [Egor Dëmin](../profiles/players/egor-demin.md), [Matas Buzelis](../profiles/players/matas-buzelis.md), [Ausar Thompson](../profiles/players/ausar-thompson.md), [Zach Edey](../profiles/players/zach-edey.md))

Treat the year-two and year-three rule as a baseline, then judge each player on his own situation. Flagg's jump is already in his price: paying above 50 USD prices it in fully. Buzelis showed few rebounds and low usage in preseason. Ausar Thompson plays for a coach with a track record of limiting minutes. Edey's upside depends on staying healthy. ## Category signals that back a breakout

In category leagues, breakouts come from efficiency at volume, a higher free throw attempt rate and a higher assist rate. Points leagues reflect these less. The same two signs, more free throws and more assists, show up before a year-three or year-four star leap, even for players who are not point guards. For non point guards, look for both rates climbing over the first six seasons. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=360), [06-30](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=258), [06-28](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1325))

The gains do not need to be big. Going from about 4 free throw attempts to 6.5 or 7 per game can move a player from around 25th to around 5th. A little better from three, a bit more usage, one extra assist and more minutes can push a player into the top 50. In our league FG% and FT% are team ratios, so efficiency only matters if it comes on real volume. ([06-28](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1354), [08-12](https://youtu.be/p9XE5jFqhvs?t=2006))

Assist-rate signals to watch: Ausar Thompson's assists moving toward 4, Buzelis taking on point forward duties, Reaves's assists without LeBron, and Miller's playmaking after Ball left. Efficiency signals to watch: Murray-Boyles's projected 58.9% FG, whether Harper keeps his roughly 50% FG, and whether Dëmin's FG% climbs from 39.9% as he takes more twos. ([Ausar Thompson](../profiles/players/ausar-thompson.md), [Matas Buzelis](../profiles/players/matas-buzelis.md), [Austin Reaves](../profiles/players/austin-reaves.md), [Brandon Miller](../profiles/players/brandon-miller.md), [Collin Murray-Boyles](../profiles/players/collin-murray-boyles.md), [Dylan Harper](../profiles/players/dylan-harper.md), [Egor Dëmin](../profiles/players/egor-demin.md))

A good per-game rank earned in limited minutes points to upside if the role grows. Kel'el Ware played 22 minutes last season and is projected for 25 to 30. Brandin Podziemski finished 136th overall but 61st after the All-Star break. Khaman Maluach played under 9 minutes and is projected for about 24. Yanic Konan Niederhäuser averaged 1.6 blocks in 17 minutes over his last seven games. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1036), [Kel'el Ware](../profiles/players/kelel-ware.md), [Brandin Podziemski](../profiles/players/brandin-podziemski.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](../profiles/players/yanic-konan-niederhauser.md))

## Where the experts disagree

The experts disagree about what drives a breakout. One view says season-level breakouts and busts come mostly from injuries and random shooting, not from changes in counting stats. On that view, look for injuries and departures and do not trust a hot preseason. The other view says you can spot real growth early through rising free throw and assist rates, and that this is how a player around 40th becomes a top 10 player. For our league, use both. Let the opening decide who goes on your list, and let free throw and assist rates decide who you keep paying for. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=436), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=360), [06-28](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1325))

They also disagree on prices. For Flagg, Josh's auction value is about 40 USD, while the sites sit near 51 to 55 USD. For Edey, bids run from Josh's 11 USD cap up to 20 USD. For Knueppel, experts call him overpriced at an ADP in the 30s and 40s, and one mock ceiling was 8 USD. When the gap is this wide, bid at the lower expert number and let others pay for the breakout. ([Cooper Flagg](../profiles/players/cooper-flagg.md), [Zach Edey](../profiles/players/zach-edey.md), [Kon Knueppel](../profiles/players/kon-knueppel.md))

## How to use this in our league

Spend your middle dollars on confirmed openings that the market has not priced yet. Buzelis is worth up to about 20 USD. Ausar Thompson is worth 15 to 18 USD. Garland is reasonable in the high teens, with 25 USD as the ceiling. Paul George is good value at 10 to 15 USD. For Reaves, 36 USD is a sensible ceiling and 40 USD is an overpay. Miller fits at about 20 to 26 USD. In a 144-player draft, the year-two flyers such as Dëmin and Murray-Boyles belong in the last dollars. ([Matas Buzelis](../profiles/players/matas-buzelis.md), [Ausar Thompson](../profiles/players/ausar-thompson.md), [Darius Garland](../profiles/players/darius-garland.md), [Paul George](../profiles/players/paul-george.md), [Austin Reaves](../profiles/players/austin-reaves.md), [Brandon Miller](../profiles/players/brandon-miller.md), [Egor Dëmin](../profiles/players/egor-demin.md), [Collin Murray-Boyles](../profiles/players/collin-murray-boyles.md))

Do not pay for a breakout from veterans. A player who has been in the league a long time and is turning 29 is probably who he is. Buy Rudy Gobert, at 34, for the extra minutes and rebounds the thin Minnesota frontcourt gives him, not for a jump. Experts see little upside in John Collins either. ([07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=837), [Rudy Gobert](../profiles/players/rudy-gobert.md), [John Collins](../profiles/players/john-collins.md))

A player's best breakout chance is the season with the most opening. When stars return, expect a step back. Plan to sell before roles shrink, and before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline. Think about selling Podziemski before Butler returns. Hachimura and Strus gain shots only while Ingram is out. Isaiah Jackson is likely a drop once Konan Niederhäuser returns. ([07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1030), [Brandin Podziemski](../profiles/players/brandin-podziemski.md), [Rui Hachimura](../profiles/players/rui-hachimura.md), [Max Strus](../profiles/players/max-strus.md), [Isaiah Jackson](../profiles/players/isaiah-jackson.md), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](../profiles/players/yanic-konan-niederhauser.md))

In the first two weeks, check minutes against each player's threshold. Examples: 28 or more for Ausar Thompson and Coward, 24 or more for Sharpe and Maluach, 30 or more for Podziemski. Cut the ones who miss, and use FAB within the 6 adds per week on players whose role grows. Examples: Joan Beringer if Gobert misses time, or Baylor Scheierman if he starts and plays 23 or more minutes.
